facts.statement: John A. Long discovered and described the type specimen of Mcnamaraspis in the Gogo Formation near Fitzroy Crossing.
facts.quote: The type specimen was found and described by John A. Long from the Gogo Formation near Fitzroy Crossing.

facts.statement: Mcnamaraspis kaprios was proclaimed the first official state fossil emblem of any Australian state on December 5, 1995.
facts.quote: On 5 December 1995, the type species, M. kaprios, was officially proclaimed as the State Fossil emblem of Western Australia by the Governor of Western Australia, thus becoming the first official state fossil emblem for any state of Australia.

facts.statement: Mcnamaraspis lived in ancient reef systems in northwestern Australia during the Frasnian epoch of the Late Devonian, approximately 380 to 375 million years ago.
facts.quote: Mcnamaraspis is an extinct monospecific genus of arthrodire placoderm that inhabited the ancient reef system of north Western Australia during the Frasnian epoch of the Late Devonian period (c. 380-375 million years ago).

facts.statement: Mcnamaraspis is sometimes called "The Gogo Fish" because its holotype was excavated from the Gogo Formation.
facts.quote: It is occasionally referred to as "The Gogo Fish" after the locale the holotype was excavated from.

facts.statement: Mcnamaraspis kaprios was a marine fish that grew to a maximum length of 0.5 meters.
facts.quote: M. kaprios is an extinct marine fish that grew up to 0.5 m in length.

facts.statement: Mcnamaraspis is inferred to have been an active predator that used its sharp, razor-like teeth to crack the shells of arthropods like trilobites.
facts.quote: With its large eyes, articulated jaw and sharp, razorlike dentition plates, it can be inferred that this midsize placoderm was an active predator that specialized in cracking through the shelled defenses of arthropods such as trilobites.

facts.statement: Mcnamaraspis possessed a distinct cartilaginous snout that has not been recorded in other placoderms.
facts.quote: It has a distinct cartilaginous snout not recorded in other placoderms.

facts.statement: Mcnamaraspis is classified within the superfamily Incisoscutoidea, the clade Coccosteomorphi, and the larger clade Eubrachythoraci.
facts.quote: Mcnamaraspis is now considered to be a member of the superfamily Incisoscutoidea, which belongs to the clade Coccosteomorphi, one of the two major clades within Eubrachythoraci.

facts.statement: The parent group for Mcnamaraspis is Incisoscutoidea.
Mcnamaraspis belongs to the class Placodermi.
The fossil record for Mcnamaraspis spans from 382.31 to 379 million years ago during the Frasnian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Frasnian to Frasnian (382.31 to 379 million years ago)
